sections.h2: Where do McMinn County owners go with property tax questions?
sections.html:
Tax bills come from the Trustee, and value questions go to the Assessor of Property. The Trustee works from the courthouse in Athens, and the County Commission sets the rate.

  • Trustee: McMinn County Courthouse, 6 East Madison Avenue, Athens, TN 37303. Phone (423) 745-1291, fax (423) 744-1603.
  • Hours: Monday to Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., plus Saturdays in February from 8:30 a.m. to noon.
  • Assessor of Property: appraises and classifies each parcel, verifies sales and handles reappraisal questions.

The Trustee's page lists the three jobs of the office: collecting county property tax, keeping the county's accounts, and investing idle funds. It also runs the state tax relief program for elderly and disabled owners and disabled veterans. Tax notices are mailed in October to whoever owned the property on January 1, and the owner is responsible for keeping the mailing address current with the Assessor.

sections.h2: What is McMinn County like for a homeowner or seller?
sections.html:
McMinn County is in East Tennessee, with Athens as the county seat and largest city. It was created in 1819 and named for Governor Joseph McMinn. It covers 432 square miles of Ridge and Valley country, where long parallel ridges run northeast to southwest. The Hiwassee River marks the line with Bradley County, and Starr Mountain rises in the southeast along the edge of the Cherokee National Forest.

Besides Athens, the county holds the cities of Etowah, Niota and Sweetwater, the towns of Calhoun and Englewood, and Riceville. Railroads shaped the early map: the East Tennessee and Georgia line ran through in the 1850s, Etowah grew around an L&N depot, and Englewood became a textile town. In 1946, returning World War II veterans confronted county officials over a disputed election in the Battle of Athens.

School lines matter here. McMinn County Schools runs most of the public schools, including McMinn County High and McMinn Central High. Athens City Schools and the Etowah School District cover grades K to 8 in their own areas, with the county's high schools taking those students after eighth grade. Tennessee Wesleyan University is in Athens.

Census Bureau QuickFacts for McMinn County:

  • Population on July 1, 2025: 57,404, up 7.8% from April 2020
  • Housing units: 24,424, with 75.8% owner-occupied from 2020 to 2024
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $211,800
  • Median gross rent: $803, and median household income $61,470
  • Building permits in 2025: 125

sections.h2: What is the McMinn County property tax rate for 2026 to 2027?
sections.html:
The combined county rate is $1.0823 per $100 of assessed value for the fiscal year that began July 1, 2026. The County Commission set it by Resolution 26-036 at its June 15, 2026 meeting, and the Trustee is authorized to round tax statements to the nearest whole dollar. Assessments follow state classes: 25 percent for farm and residential property, 30 percent for personal property, 40 percent for industrial and commercial property and 55 percent for public utilities.

The levy splits across six funds. Three of the lines carry school names: McMinn, Athens and Etowah.

As a worked example, a house appraised at $211,800, the county's median owner-occupied value, has an assessed value of $52,950. Multiply that by $1.0823 per $100 and the county tax comes to about $573. A city may add its own tax, so the figure covers county tax only.

sections.h2: When are McMinn County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Payment opens October 1 and stays open through the last day of February without penalty. Today is November 15, 2026, so the current year's tax is already payable. On March 1 the Trustee adds 1.5 percent per month in penalty and interest to unpaid tax.

Mail is accepted, and the postmark sets the payment date, with a receipt returned by mail. Delinquent tax is a lien on the property regardless of who owns it, so buyers are urged to run a title check for liens. The county also requires delinquent taxes to be paid before current ones, which means a prior-year balance absorbs a payment aimed at this year's bill.

The office also opens on Saturday mornings in February. For payment methods beyond mail and in-person, call (423) 745-1291.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a McMinn County assessment?
sections.html:
Talk to the Assessor of Property first, then file with the McMinn County Board of Equalization. State law sends a disputed value to the county board before anything else, and a case that skips it generally becomes final. The Comptroller's appeals guide explains that the county board is a panel of five or more people who hear complaints and can change disputed assessments.

  • County board: file by the date the Assessor gives you for this year's session.
  • State Board of Equalization: by August 1 of the tax year, or within 45 days of the date the county board's notice was sent, whichever is later.
  • Hearing: before an administrative judge, with a written decision within 90 days after the hearing.
  • Chancery court: a petition within 60 days after the state board's order is final.

McMinn County's FAQ adds one point for business owners. A forced assessment, which happens when a business fails to file a personal property schedule, can be set aside only by an appeal to the local board before that year's deadline. The county's FAQ says the schedule is due before March 1.

sections.h2: What property tax relief exists for McMinn County owners?
sections.html:
The Trustee administers a state-funded program for elderly and disabled homeowners and for disabled veterans. When an applicant qualifies, the State of Tennessee pays a portion of the tax on the home. The Trustee's page says an application must be filed no later than 35 days after the February 28 payment deadline, which lands in early April. The FAQ also mentions programs for veterans with a 100 percent rating.

Because income limits and credit amounts are set by the state each year, call (423) 745-1291 for this year's figures before you apply.

sections.h2: What should a McMinn County seller know about tax at closing?
sections.html:
A tax lien stays with the house, so a buyer's title search will find any unpaid year. The county says delinquent tax is a lien regardless of ownership, and a seller with a late balance should expect the title company to require payoff at closing.

Ask the Trustee for the amount for each tax year, including interest, before you accept an offer. If the house is inherited, behind on payments or in need of repairs, the tax balance is one more number the title company will collect from the proceeds, and knowing it early keeps the closing date from slipping.

faqs.q: What is the current McMinn County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The combined county rate is $1.0823 per $100 of assessed value for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2026. The County Commission adopted it on June 15, 2026. Residential property is assessed at 25 percent of appraised value.

faqs.q: When does McMinn County charge interest on late taxes?
faqs.a: On and after March 1. The Trustee adds 1.5 percent per month to delinquent tax, and payment is open from October 1 through the last day of February without penalty.

faqs.q: Can I mail my McMinn County property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Mailed payments are accepted and the postmark date decides whether you paid on time. The Trustee returns a receipt by mail.

faqs.q: Which school systems affect a McMinn County tax bill?
faqs.a: Three funds on the levy support schools: McMinn, Athens and Etowah. Athens City Schools and the Etowah School District serve grades K to 8 in their areas, while McMinn County Schools covers most of the rest.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay old McMinn County taxes before this year's?
faqs.a: Yes. The Trustee's FAQ says delinquent taxes must be paid before current taxes can be paid. A delinquent balance is also a lien on the property regardless of who owns it.
